title: Fix reentrant dispatch_sync deadlock in DefaultOutputDeviceMonitor.start()

title: Follow-main app silent after another app is redirected to This Mac
why: Reproduced live 2026-07-29 (telemetry sid C98DF1E0): with audio streaming to a Sonos Move, redirecting the only playing app to This Mac left the whole-system tap capturing and the engine writing, but the next unrouted app to press play was completely inaudible until the owner deselected and reselected the output device. Telemetry shows a measured 9.14 s gap with ZERO writes to stream 0 (send_sched gap_count frozen 15236 across 5.1 s, gap_max_ms 9136.8, write_cadence_drift deficitDeltaSeconds 9.146) starting at the exclusion-change tap teardown and ending when the second app started. The vendored sender advances RTP position by samples written (rtp_common.c:186) and builds the rtptime-to-wall-clock anchor from the producer pts on each write (airplay.c:2232,2257), so a producer stall injects a permanent skew the receiver never recovers from. resetAirPlaySessionForWholeSystem -- the only thing that re-anchors stream 0 -- has exactly two triggers (NativeBackend.swift:1389 device/rate rebuild, :2020 synced-local churn) and neither fires on write starvation. Deselect/reselect works only because it builds a brand-new session with a fresh randomized pos (rtp_common.c:75). Bug 6 in the 2026-07-26 onion chain.
what: Full investigation + fix plan: docs/plans/PLAN-REDIRECT-FOLLOW-MAIN-SILENCE.md. Investigation first, fix second. T-I1/T-I2 are owner live tests that discriminate the two surviving candidates (C1 producer-starvation gap with no re-anchor vs C2 the exclusion-change rebuild itself being unsafe to skip); T-I3 closes the observability gap (no telemetry fires when an unrouted app starts playing, and .capturing is set on tap-create success rather than first buffer); T-I4 reads the vendored sync path to decide whether a FLUSH re-anchor suffices. T-F1 (if C1) adds the missing third trigger for resetAirPlaySessionForWholeSystem, fired on the resume edge of a single long write gap, thresholded on one gap and never on cumulative deficit. NOT fixed on this branch by design -- research/plan/roadmap only, per Alec.

title: Connect-volume seed: prioritize device-reported / last-known volume over fixed default
why: Alec (2026-07-29): the connect seed today always uses a fixed connect-default (35%) on a user-initiated connect, a holdover from when the seed inherited the Macs system volume and could blast the user. He wants the priority reordered: (1) the device/system own reported current volume if available, (2) otherwise the level that device previously had in our system, persisted per device across restarts, (3) the fixed connect-default only as a last resort for a never-seen device. Only the user-connect branch changes; F-REBIND (out-of-band reconnect) already preserves the in-session level and is untouched.
what: Read-only research + plan: docs/plans/PLAN-CONNECT-VOLUME-SEED.md. Traces the current seed (NativeBackend.connectVolumeSeed, userConnectSeed, stashedVolume, known[id].volume), the wire/UI domain conversion setSpeakerVolume already demonstrates for a receiver-reported level, and the vendored AirPlay sender/receiver protocol. Feasibility verdict: no GET_PARAMETER or any pull primitive exists anywhere in the vendored C sender (0 matches); the sender is the protocols volume authority and only ever pushes SET_PARAMETER. The only receiver-volume signal is an asynchronous, receiver-initiated push (RTSP reverse /event channel or DACP setproperty, both already wired to NativeBackend), coded and documented as a change notification, not an initial-state announcement; whether any receiver fires one unprompted at connect time, early enough to beat the seeds own push, is unverified and needs a live hardware probe (T-I1). Persistence finding: known[id].volume and stashedVolume are in-memory only today, nothing is written to disk, so tier 2 (persisted last-known level) is new work, not a rename -- DeviceIconStore.swift is the direct pattern to copy (stable colon-hex device id, Codable versioned JSON, same Application Support directory). Also raises, without deciding, an anti-blast open question: a device reporting 100% reopens the exact blast risk the fixed default was built to close, so the plan proposes T-I2 as an owner decision between trusting tier 1 unclamped, a cheap ceiling clamp, or a genuine ramp. Task list separates investigation-remaining (T-I1 live protocol probe, T-I2 anti-blast decision) from implementation (T-F1 bounded-listen tier-1 mechanism, T-F2 DeviceVolumeStore, T-F3 write-through wiring, T-F4 rewire connectVolumeSeed, T-F5 tests, T-F6 docs), gated on the two owner decisions.
notes: 2026-07-29 Read-only research on claude/connect-volume-seed (worktree .claude/worktrees/connect-volume-seed, off main@2042de1). No code changed, no live test run by the agent. Two things need the owner before implementation starts: T-I1 (does any target receiver report its own volume unprompted, early enough in the connect sequence to use) and T-I2 (the anti-blast clamp-vs-ramp-vs-trust decision for a device-reported value). DeviceVolumeStore (T-F2) is independent of both and can be built in parallel.

title: BT-mic (HFP) trigger causes app<->Bluetooth rebuild oscillation with audible drops
why: Reproduced live 2026-07-29 ~19:40 (telemetry sid C98DF1E0): triggering the Bluetooth microphone (HFP mode) while streaming caused a rebuild ping-pong — 16000Hz rebuild+session_reset at 19:40:01, 44100Hz rebuild+session_reset at 19:40:23, another device_change + rebuild 2s later with rebind_recover_flush noop_fallback. Each of our tap rebuilds touches the BT device mid-renegotiation, likely re-perturbing it (our private tap-aggregate includes the BT device as a whole sub-device, input side unrestricted — NativeCaptureCoordinator.swift createAggregate ~:2263 — so aggregate IO may itself engage the mic path and force/prolong HFP). Owner: big drop + back-and-forth disconnect between app and Bluetooth; not urgent but must be addressed.
notes:
Same BT/HFP family as the 16kHz corpse-pin found the same evening (rebuild during BT teardown pinned capture at 16000 for 16s) and shares fix surface with docs/plans/PLAN-CONSISTENT-MAINOUT-RATE-PIN.md (on main) and roadmap 016/017. Candidate directions: treat 16000Hz as a known HFP settling marker and defer rebuilds while the device renegotiates; widen/rate-aware settle window for HFP transitions; restrict the tap-aggregate sub-device to output streams so our own IO cannot engage the BT mic. Evidence preserved in telemetry sid C98DF1E0 19:40:01-19:40:27.
2026-08-07 === RE-REPRODUCED LIVE 2026-08-07 ~01:45Z, with the cost measured. Read this before starting. ===

TRIGGER (takes ~1 min, fully reliable): connect WH-1000XM3 as the Mac's system output, stream
whole-system audio to an AirPlay speaker (Sonos Move 2, C4:38:75:0E:BF:4A), then open the mic
(FaceTime / Voice Memos record / Photo Booth). The headset's OUTPUT device collapses
44100 -> 16000 on mic-open and recovers 16000 -> 44100 on mic-close (HFP hands-free), ~14 s apart.
NOTE: the headset exposes output and mic as SEPARATE CoreAudio devices (CC-98-8B-93-16-55:output /
:input); the :input device sits at 16000 permanently and is NOT the trigger. The OUTPUT device
collapsing is. Also note AudioObjectIDs are per-HAL-client: the app logged this device as 167 while
an external probe saw 107 - do not try to correlate raw IDs across processes.

MEASURED COST (new netDriftSeconds counter, landed on claude/cadence-counter-fix):
  before mic:  net 7.745, flat across 5 windows
  mic opens:   net 8.220  (+0.475 s)
  mic closes:  net 8.927  (+0.708 s)
  after:       net 8.927, flat across 8 windows
  => 1.18 s of audio lost per mic toggle, in two discrete jumps, nothing in between.
Each edge does aggregate_destroy + create_and_start + format_reconciled + a full AirPlay
session_reset(recovery=flush_first) + rebind + rebind_recover_flush. send_sched gap_max goes
11.9 ms -> 493.8 ms (open) and 563.8 ms (close).

SECOND DEFECT, arguably worse, found the same run: for the ENTIRE 16 kHz window the app follows the
device down and streams 16 kHz upsampled audio to the AirPlay speaker - transition logs
"16000/2 creatingTap -> capturing", format_reconciled {aggregateRate:16000, declaredRate:48000},
send_sched gap_p50 shifts 11.6 -> 20.0 ms for the whole window. So the speaker gets materially
degraded audio for as long as the mic is open, not just a gap at each edge. Fix direction: do not
adopt the output device's nominal rate as the capture rate when that rate is an HFP artifact
(16000 on a device that was 44100/48000 a moment ago is the marker). This is separate from the
rebuild cost and may be the more user-visible half.

THIRD, OPEN AND UNCAUSED - please investigate as part of this entry: playback volume audibly
INCREASES while the mic is active, and returns to normal when it closes (owner-reported, same run).
Channel count stays stereo throughout (16000/2), so mono-being-duplicated-into-both-channels is
RULED OUT. No cause established. Cheapest next step is an isolation test: play to the headset
WITHOUT routing through the app and open the mic - if it still gets louder it is macOS's HFP volume
curve and out of our hands; if it only happens through the app it is ours. Untested either way.

CORRECTIONS to this entry's original "why" - two prior hypotheses now have evidence against them:
1. "Our tap rebuilds re-perturb the device, causing a ping-pong." NOT what happens now. The 2026-08-07
   run shows exactly 2 fires for 1 mic toggle - one per real edge - with duplicate notifications
   correctly coalesced (default_output_change fired=1/1 then fired=0/1 on each edge). The shared
   debounced monitor + TapRebuildDecision compare-before-rebuild guard in DefaultOutputDeviceMonitor
   ARE applied and work correctly. Do NOT re-implement them. The rate change is genuine and external;
   no guard can suppress it, only make it cheaper or ignorable.
2. "Our private tap-aggregate includes the BT device input-side unrestricted, so our own IO may engage
   the mic path and force/prolong HFP." Every whole-system aggregate_create in the reproduction logs
   inputStreams:0, outputStreams:1 - evidence against, though I did not read createAggregate's
   sub-device config to confirm, so treat as strong hint rather than disproof.

METHOD NOTE for whoever picks this up: absence of rate flips in telemetry does NOT mean fixed. This
entry looked dormant for 9 days (zero flips 07-29..08-06) purely because nobody had opened a mic
while connected. Reproduce before concluding anything.

MEASURE IT WITH: netDriftTotalSeconds / netDriftDeltaSeconds / stalledTotalSeconds / stallCount on
the write_cadence_drift event (claude/cadence-counter-fix, AirPlayEngine.swift WriteCadenceTracker +
AirPlayTypes.swift WriteCadenceSnapshot). Do NOT use deficitTotalSeconds alone - it is a one-sided sum
that inflates under ordinary jitter and separately swallows pauses/sleeps.
2026-08-07 DEFECT 2 FIXED (branch claude/hfp-rate-pin, 8612ca7c, NOT merged, live verification owed).

WHAT SHIPPED. CoreAudioSystemTap.isHandsFreeArtifactRate(transport:rate:) marks the HFP state as Bluetooth transport + rate <= 16000 (8 kHz CVSD / 16 kHz mSBC). On that marker createAggregate adds kAudioSubDeviceDriftCompensationKey to the sub-DEVICE entry and setNominalSampleRate() holds the private aggregate at PCMFormat.airplay.sampleRate (44100). Write targets OUR aggregate only, never the user's device. New telemetry hfp_rate_pin {deviceRate, requested, readBack, status}. Kill switch AUDIOUTER_HFP_RATE_PIN=0 (default ON). Whole-system only; per-app is a marked razor: ceiling.

DESIGN ANSWER - "recent healthy rate" is NOT remembered, deliberately. A Bluetooth OUTPUT device at <=16 kHz IS in hands-free mode, so transport+rate carries the same information as rate history with no state, no expiry, no clock, and nothing that must survive a tap rebuild. Yield-to-evidence needs no timer either: if the pin is refused, reconcileFormatWithAggregate reads the real aggregate rate and the pipeline degrades to follow-the-device automatically. Ceiling + upgrade path (remember last non-hands-free rate per device UID on the coordinator) are in a razor: comment at the marker.

DEFECT-1 IMPACT: NONE. The pin does not reduce the 1.18 s. Both edges still rebuild. It first looked as though the close edge would vanish (tracked format 44100 == recovered device 44100 => no divergence => no fire), but that "win" was an artifact of the guard comparing the wrong quantity: with format reported as tracked, a pinned tap reads as DIVERGED against the 16 kHz device on EVERY notification for the whole call, and each rebuild perturbs the device into posting the next one - a self-feeding storm, exactly what TapRebuildDecision exists to break. Fixed by reporting the DEVICE's rate as of tap build (new CoreAudioSystemTap.tappedDeviceRate, sampled beside the aggregate read). Test pinnedTapIgnoresReAnnouncementsWhileTheDeviceHoldsItsHandsFreeRate proves it; reverting the one line makes it fire 3 rebuilds instead of 0. Killing the two edge rebuilds is plan section 3 Part 2 and must NOT ship on hermetic evidence: the capture path has NO all-zero-PCM detector (the silence watchdog is connection-state based, NativeBackend.swift:5277-5301), so a wrongly suppressed rebuild is silent-forever with no net.

DEFECT 3 - code-level only, 5 hypotheses, ranked:
H1 (~80%, by far the strongest). The HFP volume scalar is read as a USER GESTURE and becomes Main Out master gain, multiplying every AirPlay device. macOS keeps separate volume state for a device's HFP vs A2DP mode; the profile switch fires the scalar listener, and the handler reports it with defaultDeviceChanged:false - i.e. as deliberate intent. Chain: SystemOutputVolume.swift:202-207 + :513-533 (listener on the default device's volume scalar) -> :336-352 (read) -> :607-614 (fires as a gesture) -> NativeBackend.swift:1388 -> :1444-1446 (the only filter; both its conditions PASS here) -> AudiouterApp/AppDelegate.swift:1314,:1329 -> GroupController.swift:846-848 -> :817-828 -> :808-812 -> NativeBackend.swift:1984-2001 -> multiply at :6394-6395, masterGainFraction :6417-6419. The design's own safeguard (SystemOutputVolume.swift:49-62) exists to stop exactly this class of event but keys on defaultDeviceChanged, and an HFP swap does not change the device id. Direction matches (HFP volume is usually near max) and it reverses at mic close.
H2 (~35%) Break-before-make unmute on repeated rebuilds: same-device rate rebuild tears down first (NativeCaptureCoordinator.swift:1163-1168, :1178), leaving the headset untapped and therefore UNMUTED (tap is .mutedWhenTapped, :382,:441) - the file names this leak itself at :1147-1161. NOTE: the storm fix above removes the repeat-rebuild driver, so this should now be at most two blips.
H3 (~20% sustained) Same mechanism at just the two edges; becomes sustained only if the tap fails to come back up at 16 kHz (validate only rejects rate <= 0, :715-720).
H4 (~10%) Silence watchdog un-gates capture, making the Mac audible (NativeBackend.swift:5346-5357, gate :6698-6699) - needs a full disconnect, which the flush path :3327-3334 avoids.
H5 (~3%) AP1-vs-AP2 volume curve flip across a rebind is an ~11 dB jump at an unchanged slider (NativeBackend.swift:6396, :6411-6413, :6367-6373); nothing ties it to a BT profile switch.
REFUTED WITH EVIDENCE: (a) session reset/rebind re-sending or resetting volume - the reset prefers an in-place flush that touches no volume (:3327-3341), and connectVolumeSeed takes the PRESERVE branch for any non-user add (:6638-6641); (b) reconciledFormat buffer reinterpretation as a LEVEL change - it rewrites only sampleRate (:2634-2644) and the IOProc walk is rate-independent (:2514-2516, :2556-2576); (c) resampler/channel-sum gain - plain AVAudioConverter with no gain stage (:3184-3245), AppRouteMixer never sees stream 0 (AppRouteMixer.swift:26-28), SyncedLocalSink excludes Main (:212-215).

LIVE CHECKLIST (owner; single-instance rule, sweep stale PTP helpers first; build via scripts/make-app.sh):
1. Baseline AUDIOUTER_HFP_RATE_PIN=0, then pinned (default). Same trigger as before: WH-1000XM3 as system output + whole-system to the Sonos, open FaceTime/Voice Memos ~15 s, close.
2. PIN HELD? grep hfp_rate_pin - readBack must be 44100 and status 0. If readBack is 16000 the pin was refused: try plan section 5 Variant C (kAudioAggregateDeviceClockDeviceKey / no main sub-device).
3. DEFECT 2 GONE? format_reconciled must NOT show aggregateRate:16000 during the window, and the transition log must not read "16000/2 creatingTap". send_sched gap_p50 should stay ~11.6 ms instead of moving to 20.0 ms.
4. DID THE PIN DRAG THE HEADSET? aggregate_create's rateAfterCreate (physical device) - it must stay 16000. If it jumps to 44100 we are fighting the OS mid-call: check the call audio is still sane.
5. LISTEN for chipmunk/fast audio. Pin held + tap genuinely delivering at a 16 kHz cadence would run ~2.76x fast. That is the one failure the hermetic tests cannot see. If heard: revert to follow-the-device (=0) and report; the pin's premise is wrong.
6. NO STORM: default_output_change fired= counts must still be 2 per mic toggle, and rate_changed_rebuild_triggered must not repeat during the window.
7. COST: read netDriftTotalSeconds / netDriftDeltaSeconds / stalledTotalSeconds / stallCount on write_cadence_drift (never deficitTotalSeconds alone). Expect ~1.18 s per toggle UNCHANGED - the pin does not address defect 1.
8. DEFECT 3, one glance decides H1: watch the Main Out readout/slider (and AppSettings.mainOutVolume) across the mic window. Jumps up on open + returns on close => H1 confirmed, no audio analysis needed. Rock-steady => H1 killed, fall through to counting rebuild telemetry (H2/H3), then the "playing on this Mac" banner (H4).

title: Per-app tap make-before-break on default-device change

title: Same-device AirPlay handoff: yield the speaker instead of fighting for it
why: Live-found 2026-08-07 (Alec, handoff live test). Releasing the PTP ports is enough only when macOS wants a DIFFERENT speaker. When Sound settings selects the SAME speaker Audiouter is streaming to, macOS also needs that speakers RTSP session, and AirPlay receivers accept one sender at a time — so it fails kIOReturnExclusiveAccess on every attempt (confirmed 4/4 against Sonos Move at 02:20:04/08/12/18 while telemetry showed us holding 54:2A:1B:79:08:9E). Intent-preservation then makes any resume re-grab the same speaker, so the user can never win it. Different-device handoff already passes (A/A2/C/C2 all verified).
what: Alec chose Option 2 (yield temporarily, do NOT auto-resume). Detect that macOS is targeting a speaker we currently stream to: the unified-log line that already drives the watcher carries the target name unredacted (subsystem com.apple.airplay, category APSenderSessionAirPlay: Connect over DirectLink with "<name>"), so BlockedAirPlayAttempt can extract it and NativeBackend can compare against the streaming set. On a same-device match: release the PTP ports AND tear down that speakers session, then leave it released — suppress the D1 .stillOurs resume and the button-free auto-resume for that device specifically, and surface the existing routing-blocked banner so the user takes it back deliberately via Use Audiouter. Keep the current behaviour untouched for different-device. Entry points: AirPlayHandoffWatcher/BlockedAirPlayAttempt (matcher, add target-name capture), NativeBackend.releaseForHandoff + resumeFromHandoffLocked + the defaultLeftUsSinceRelease gate (already added for the bounce-back loop), PopoverController routing-blocked banner. Needs a live re-test with two speakers (same-device AND different-device paths).
